title: Best Time to Visit Kornati, Croatia: Seasonal Guide 2027
metaDescription: When to visit Kornati: late May to mid-June and September balance weather, crowds and park fees. Season verdicts, ticket costs and local tips for 2027.
content:
## Best Time to Visit Kornati: The Verdict

Late May to mid-June and the whole of September are the best windows for Kornati. In both periods the air and sea are warm, the northern Dalmatian winds are usually manageable, and the archipelago is far less busy than in July and August. Kornati National Park is open year-round by boat. In practice, the usable season runs from about April to October, because off-season many facilities close and overnight stays are limited.

The pick between the two windows depends on priorities:

- **Choose September** for swimming. The sea has had all summer to warm up, and it is the most reliable month for a swim-focused trip.
- **Choose late May to mid-June** for long daylight, green island vegetation and the lowest crowds relative to weather quality.
- **Choose July or August** only if fixed school holidays or the warmest possible sea matter more than space and price. The reduced-crowd argument for this period does not exist.

## How the Seasons Compare

### Spring (April to mid-June)

Spring works well for sailors and photographers. Light is clear, temperatures are comfortable for hiking the islands, and anchorages are often nearly empty. The trade-off is that mooring buoys and some seasonal konobas may not be in place in April and early May, so a boat may need to rely on its own anchor. Swimming is possible but the sea is cool early on.

### Summer (late June to August)

This is the high season for park fees, charter rates and excursion traffic. Day-trip boats from Zadar, Šibenik, Murter, Vodice and Biograd all run daily. Bays such as Ravni Žakan turn into small tourist hubs when excursion boats arrive around midday. Decisive recommendation: for anyone with flexible dates, skipping the last two weeks of July and the first three of August is the single best change to make.

### Early autumn (September to early October)

Autumn gives warm water, softer light and fewer boats. Services thin out gradually through October. The park's peak-season tariff applies until September 30, so entry is still at the higher rate for most of September, but the lower crowd level and cheaper charters offset it.

### Winter (November to March)

Winter is for people who want solitude and accept the limits. Weather is unsettled, strong bura winds can make crossings uncomfortable, and most restaurants and marinas are closed. Organised day tours are not a reliable option.

## What It Costs: Park Fees by Season

Kornati admission is charged per boat, per day, not per person. The park uses a pre-season rate and a higher season rate. The season tariff applies from June 1 to September 30.

| Boat length | Pre-season, 1 day | Season, 1 day |
|---|---|---|
| Under 7 m | €25 | €45 |
| 7–11 m | €30 | €65 |
| 11–18 m | €50 | €95 |

Multi-day tickets cut the daily cost. Tickets bought from ranger boats inside the park cost roughly double the advance price for the smallest class (€45 or €90 per day), so buying online before sailing is the better move. A fishing licence costs €20 for one day or €40 for three days, on top of the boat ticket.

### Day-trip passengers

Passengers on organised tours pay no separate park fee. Full-day tours from Zadar and Šibenik generally cost about €35–60 per person and include the boat, lunch and park ticket. Private skippered RIB tours cost about €950 per boat for up to 11 guests.

## Weather and Wind: What Matters for Timing

The maestral is the usual summer westerly, steady in the afternoon and reliable for sailing. The bura, a cold northerly, is the main hazard and is more common outside summer. The jugo, a southeasterly, brings rougher seas and low cloud. ACI marina Piškera can be approached safely only from the south, and in a mistral or strong southerly the channel is unsafe. Because of this, shoulder-season trips benefit from a flexible itinerary.

## Best Time by Traveller Type

- **Sailors and charter crews:** Late May to mid-June and September. Pre-season rates, quieter anchorages and fewer boats on popular buoys.
- **Swimmers and snorkellers:** September, then late June.
- **Day-trippers:** Late May to June and September. Tours run most days, with less crowding at lunch stops.
- **Families with school-age children:** July and August are usually the only choice. Book boats and konoba tables early.
- **Photographers and hikers:** April to early June, for clear light and cooler temperatures on the exposed limestone.
- **Budget travellers:** Late May and October. The pre-season tariff cuts park fees roughly in half.

## Local Tips for Timing a Trip

- **Start early.** In summer, leave harbour before 9:00 to reach the outer islands and crowns (the dramatic cliffs on the seaward side) before tour boats arrive.
- **Buy the ticket before the date change.** A ticket's category depends on the date of use, so a trip that straddles June 1 or September 30 should be planned around the tariff.
- **Check for buoys in spring.** In April and May, assume anchoring may be necessary and carry spare anchor gear.
- **Book konobas ahead.** Restaurants in Vrulje, Strižnja and on Vela Smokvica, Lavsa and Katina operate in season only. Call ahead outside July and August to confirm they are open.
- **Avoid night navigation.** Local knowledge is needed in the archipelago after dark, so plan to be moored by late afternoon.

## Bottom Line

For most travellers, September is the safest choice, and late May to mid-June is the best value. Both avoid the crowding and cost of mid-summer while keeping weather, services and water temperature at a good level.

faq.question: What is the best month to visit Kornati?
faq.answer: September is the best single month for most visitors, thanks to warm water, lighter traffic and stable weather. Late May to mid-June is a close second and is better for long days and lower park fees.

faq.question: Is Kornati National Park open in winter?
faq.answer: Yes, the park is open year-round by boat, with no gates or fixed hours. However, most konobas and facilities close in winter, and weather is unpredictable, so April to October is the realistic visiting window.

faq.question: How much does it cost to enter Kornati National Park?
faq.answer: Admission is charged per boat, per day. A 7–11 m boat pays about €30 in pre-season and €65 in season, and an 11–18 m boat pays about €50 or €95. Passengers on organised day tours pay no separate fee.

faq.question: When is Kornati most crowded?
faq.answer: July and August are the busiest months, when excursion boats and charter yachts fill the popular bays. Arriving before 9:00 or visiting the outer islands helps avoid the midday peak.

faq.question: Is it cheaper to visit Kornati outside summer?
faq.answer: Yes. The park's season tariff applies from June 1 to September 30 and is roughly double the pre-season price. Charter rates also fall in spring and autumn.

faq.question: Can you visit Kornati without your own boat?
faq.answer: Yes. Day tours run from Zadar, Šibenik, Murter, Vodice, Biograd and Pakoštane for roughly €35–60 per person, including the boat, lunch and park ticket. There is no bridge or scheduled ferry to the archipelago.

quickAnswer: The best time to visit Kornati is late May to mid-June and September. The sea is warm enough to swim, most konobas and moorings are running, and boat traffic is lighter than in July and August. Park tickets also cost about half as much before June 1 and after September 30.
